candidates.concept: BIG QUESTION, THEN THE TANK DRAINS
candidates.metaphor: A huge question mark hangs in the dark; directly beneath it an energy gauge runs from full to nearly empty, so the act of asking is visibly costing charge.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The headline poses the hook while the ProgressBar empties top-to-bottom in the same frame — depletion is enacted, not named: the viewer watches energy leave.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Emptying bar + tiredness words = the thing being asked about is exhausting. Even muted, a gauge hitting zero reads as 'running out'.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Uppercase headline with accentWords ['paling','capek'] in gold; caption reads the drain label.
candidates.motionOpportunity: WordReveal stagger on entrance, then a single controlled drain of the bar; caption fades last.
candidates.whyItWorks: Directly maps the metaphorHints (question mark, drained energy) into one vertical axis, keeping only two elements and huge negative space.

candidates.concept: ONE POINT OF LIGHT THAT ASKS
candidates.metaphor: The frame is almost entirely void; one small glowing dot is the only light, and the question grows out of it like the curve of a '?' — curiosity as the single surviving spark.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Total darkness vs one live dot: the question is the only thing still burning, physically isolating 'penasaran' inside 'kelelahan'.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A lone light in blackness reads as the last bit of attention/curiosity — the eye goes there, then the question appears from it.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Centered headline emerging from the dot, accentWords ['paling','capek'] in gold.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Dot fades in first (fade), glow stays subordinate intensity ≤0.4, then WordReveal grows upward word by word.
candidates.whyItWorks: Simplest possible hierarchy: one light, one question. Maximum stillness for a 3.6s hook.

candidates.metaphor: On the right, a stack of eight charged bars; while the question is read, members of the stack drop out one by one until only two remain — energy as a counted, finite pile.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Accumulation reversed: the stack physically loses countable units in sequence, so 'bikin capek' becomes a subtraction event the viewer tracks.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Blocks disappearing from a stack is universally 'using up' — the shrinking pile under a fatigue question needs no narration.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Left-aligned headline, gold accent on 'capek'; small uppercase label under the stack reads ENERGI.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger exit on stack members (fade), headline reveals first, label highlights at the last drop.
candidates.whyItWorks: Gives the right half a real event instead of decoration, and the countable loss differs from every prior bar/gauge idea in memory.

candidates.metaphor: A long hairline arrow pushes right toward a hollow dot, but its tail thins and dissolves before reaching — the effort is real, the arrival never happens.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Two competing states on one axis: forward motion vs retraction. The gap that stays open despite motion is the definition of tiring struggle.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Something moving toward a target yet never touching it reads instantly as endless trying — the question simply names it.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline set low-left, uppercase, accentWords ['paling','capek'] gold; one muted caption under the target dot.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Arrow draws in (draw), target dot pulses once (subtleScale), hairline fades — max two motion systems.
candidates.whyItWorks: Enacts exhaustion as a geometry problem and stays visually distinct from all gauge/stack/light candidates.

candidates.concept: THE COUNTER BLED DOWN TO EMPTY
candidates.metaphor: A single huge number counts itself down from 100 toward single digits under the question, a ring around it dimming in sync — fatigue shown as a measurable drain.
candidates.semanticMechanism: counterChange makes time/energy loss literal: the number visibly falls while the viewer reads, so the frame is doing the meaning.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A collapsing percentage under 'paling bikin capek' is read as 'how much is left' — universally decoded as running out.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline top-left with gold accent on 'capek', giant counter as the second tier, caption as unit label.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Counter runs its duration inside the scene; ring dims with highlight; headline reveals first then counter starts.
candidates.whyItWorks: Number-led tier (counter 140px) gives a strong cold-open graphic that no prior project used for a fatigue hook.

candidates.metaphor: A mirror ring keeps re-drawing itself at different diameters; the reflection inside never holds still, checking appearance over and over for approval.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The same Circle outline redraws at three different sizes in a loop while the label under it flips between verdicts — self re-checking, never fixed.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A face-frame that keeps resizing and a label that keeps changing reads instantly as someone unable to stop checking how they look.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline 96px Archivo uppercase left, two accent words on 'DIJAGA'; micro-label under mirror cycles verdicts.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger on headline, subtleScale redraw of the ring, highlight on the verdict label, fade out.
candidates.whyItWorks: It performs the anxiety loop physically: the check itself, not the result, is the subject.

candidates.metaphor: A spoken line leaves the mouth straight but is re-angled at three checkpoints, exiting as a cautious zigzag instead of its own direction.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The Arrow's own trajectory is visibly re-drawn mid-path — each checkpoint rotates the next segment, so the meaning performs self-editing before the words get out.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A line that starts straight and keeps getting kinked by markers reads as words being rewritten on the way to someone else.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline 96px left, accent on 'DIJAGA'; small labels at each checkpoint name the filter.
candidates.motionOpportunity: reveal of segments in sequence, positionShift at each correction, fade of the original straight ghost line.
candidates.whyItWorks: Enacts the cost directly: the sentence arrives, but not as itself.

candidates.metaphor: A stack of cards keeps cycling its top card — each version briefly accepted, then replaced — while the person underneath never changes.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Repeated replacement of the highlighted top element in the same slot shows appearance being re-decided repeatedly with no settled result.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A deck whose top card keeps flipping in the same spot reads as endless re-deciding about how to appear.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline 96px uppercase left with one gold accent word, caption 30px explaining the loop.
candidates.motionOpportunity: staggered swaps of the active card, highlight on the top card, fade on discarded versions.
candidates.whyItWorks: Turns 'dipikirin' into a visible repeated action instead of a stated idea.

candidates.concept: SELF DOT RE-CENTERS ON EVERY RING
candidates.metaphor: One small dot abandons its own position and jumps to the exact center of each passing ring, never staying where it started.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The same subject object repeatedly positionShifts to satisfy a different external frame, so identity literally moves wherever validation points.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Watching the dot chase each ring's center shows someone reshaping themselves for whoever is watching.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline 96px left, accent words 'SEMUA ORANG'; label under active ring shows the current demand.
candidates.motionOpportunity: positionShift of the dot between centers, subtleScale on the active ring, controlledReveal of demands.
candidates.whyItWorks: Performs the impossible task: satisfying several centers at once means never having one of your own.

candidates.metaphor: A split board: on the left the raw self in plain marks, on the right the same marks re-arranged to fit a target shape, with one side dimming as the other brightens.
candidates.semanticMechanism: A direct side-by-side where the tuned column brightens while the true column dims, showing approval is purchased by subtraction.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Two versions of one thing, one visibly preferred over the other, communicates editing for acceptance without narration.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline 96px uppercase, one accent word per column label, caption 30px closing line.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger reveal of both columns, highlight on the tuned side, fade down of the true side.
candidates.whyItWorks: Gives the abstract idea a measurable, countable contrast while keeping the palette to one dominant accent.

candidates.metaphor: A composed post card sits under a views-counter stuck at 0, then dissolves on its own — no audience ever arrived.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Independent confirmation: the read-counter never leaves 0 while the card dissolves, proving the deletion happened before any judgment could exist.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A disappearing post above '0' reads reads as self-erasure: it was never seen, so the fear deleted it, not the audience.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Left headline 'POSTING… HAPUS LAGI' with gold accent on 'HAPUS LAGI'; small muted label under the card.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Card entrance fade, emphasis on counter stuck at 0, card exit dissolve — one motion system at a time.
candidates.whyItWorks: It performs the paradox of preemptive self-censorship with countable evidence instead of naming it.

candidates.concept: HOLLOW WATCHERS GATHER AROUND ONE TILE
candidates.metaphor: A small bright post tile sits center while hollow outline circles — imaginary judges — pop in around it and dim it by presence alone.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Watchers are drawn as unfilled outlines (not real), yet the post loses brightness as they accumulate: imagined judgment has real effect.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Empty rings crowding a single glowing card read as eyes that aren't really there but still make the post shrink back.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Centered subheadline above the cluster, max one accent word in red for 'NGEJUDGE'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Stagger entrance for circles, subtleScale emphasis on the card dimming, glow stays subordinate.
candidates.whyItWorks: Contrasts real object vs hollow spectator geometry — the fear is visible while remaining literally empty.

candidates.metaphor: A line of draft text reveals word by word, then erases itself backwards word by word until only a blinking cursor remains.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The same content is enacted twice in opposite directions: creation is fully performed, then fully undone — nothing reaches the outside.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Watching a sentence take itself back is instantly decoded as typing-then-deleting, no icon needed.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Draft sentence in quote tier, headline tier below in uppercase with gold accent on 'HAPUS LAGI'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: WordReveal stagger in, staggered fade exit in reverse order, cursor Indicator emphasis highlight.
candidates.whyItWorks: Typography itself becomes the victim, so the type system carries the emotional event rather than decorating it.

candidates.metaphor: A post card slides toward a publish arrow, stops a hair short of the line, then slides all the way back to where it started.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Approach-and-withdrawal trajectory: the distance closed is visually measured and then returned to zero, showing the attempt cancelled from inside.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Any object that starts toward an exit and comes back reads as hesitation without needing a single word.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Right-aligned headline pair: 'MAU POST' muted, then 'BATAL LAGI' in red accent, two accent words max.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Slide entrance, positionShift emphasis at the threshold, slide exit back — single motion system.
candidates.whyItWorks: Motion, not iconography, carries the meaning; the threshold line makes the near-miss measurable.

candidates.concept: STACK OF DELETED DRAFTS, ZERO SENT
candidates.metaphor: Muted draft cards pile downward one after another while a 'terkirim' counter stays locked at 0.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Two counters in opposition: deletions accumulate visibly, published count never moves — effort rises, output remains zero.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A growing stack next to an unmoving zero reads instantly as repeated tries that never left the room.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Left headline max 3 lines with gold accent on one key word; counter in counter tier.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Stagger entrance for stack layers, counterChange emphasis on deletions, fade on published counter.
candidates.whyItWorks: Quantifies a loop of hesitation and stays distinct from gate/loop metaphors used in prior projects.

candidates.concept: ARROWS FROM EVERY DIRECTION MISS ONE MARK
candidates.metaphor: A single outlined target sits still while arrows arrive from all compass directions; none can cover every approach at once — each angle leaves a gap.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The target never changes, yet arrows arrive from mutually exclusive directions; no single arrangement can block all approaches, so disapproval is structurally unavoidable regardless of effort.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Seeing arrows strike from opposing sides while empty gaps remain between them reads instantly: one target cannot face every critic simultaneously.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline uppercase left-aligned near top, emphasis phrase 'pasti ada aja yang nggak suka' in gold, max 2 accent words.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Arrows stagger in from distinct angles (stagger), target holds with subtleScale, headline word-reveal then fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Physically enacts 'impossible to satisfy all sides' as geometry rather than stating it; distinct from prior arrow-converge and needle-flip motifs by focusing on un-blockable angles.

candidates.concept: WEIGHT ALWAYS SIDES WITH THE NEXT VOICE
candidates.metaphor: A balance beam tips fully to whichever side a new judgment token lands last, swinging back the moment an opposite judgment arrives.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Each new opinion drops onto alternating pans and the beam immediately swings to that side — no stable equilibrium exists, so effort cannot settle the scale.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A scale that keeps flipping to the newest weight shows the verdict was never about the object being weighed.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline split above/below beam, emphasis phrase in gold; supporting line secondary tier, left aligned.
candidates.motionOpportunity: positionShift beam tilt alternating, stagger tokens dropping, fade exit.
candidates.whyItWorks: Directly performs the 'timbangan selalu berat sebelah' hint; the swinging reversal embodies judgment reversal, distinct from static arrow imagery.

candidates.concept: THE MOVING X NEVER STAYS NAILED
candidates.metaphor: A hand-drawn X marks where approval 'should' land, but the mark slides aside each time; the crosshair chases a target that relocates on every attempt.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Effort corrects toward the mark, the mark relocates, distance never closes — repeating chase proves the success condition is controlled by the judge, not the actor.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Watching a target dodge its own aiming point makes 'you can't win no matter what you do' visible without narration.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Left column headline two lines max, emphasis gold; right side object dominates.
candidates.motionOpportunity: positionShift mark relocation each beat, controlledReveal arrow path, fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Shows effort-vs-judgment asymmetry as motion; distinct grammar (leftTextRightObject) and object set from c1/c2.

candidates.concept: EVERY PATH ARRIVES AT A DIFFERENT VERDICT
candidates.metaphor: Four approach lines radiate inward from different starting points but each terminates at its own labeled verdict, never converging into one acceptance.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Convergent effort lines fail to merge: each route ends in a separate negative verdict, so no combination of behaviors yields a single unanimous outcome.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Branches that refuse to merge while carrying opposite verdicts telegraph 'no matter which way you go, criticism waits.'
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline upper-left, verdict labels as micro-label tier under each branch end, emphasis gold on phrase.
candidates.motionOpportunity: draw branch lines sequentially, highlight each verdict, fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Uses diagram grammar unfamiliar in memory for this project; multiple contradictory outcomes shown as one static structure.

candidates.metaphor: A central circle is ringed by three labels arriving at once — 'too much', 'too little', 'wrong' — each firing from its own side with no pause between them.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Judgments fire simultaneously and contradictorily, so satisfying one provokes another; the center has no state that satisfies all three at once.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Simultaneous contradictory labels around one still dot reads as: any choice offends somebody.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline bottom-left above margin, emphasis gold; badges as pill accents with red reserved only for the contradiction word.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger badges appearing, subtleScale circle holding, fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Contradiction made spatial rather than sequential; lightweight and legible at short duration, low clutter.

candidates.metaphor: Left column: four honest actions. Right column: four accusations. Every row's verdict sits offset, never level with its cause.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The Comparison diagram maps input to output four times; staggered offsets make it physically impossible for any action to land on a matching verdict — misalignment IS the injustice, visible before any word is read.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Four clean causes on one side, four hostile effects on the other, none level with each other: nothing you do lines up with what you get.
candidates.typographyStrategy: WordReveal headline 'LU BAIK = PENCITRAAN' style pairing, only the four verdict words in red, caption carries the blow.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Rows stagger in left-to-right, then right labels shift vertically out of alignment (positionShift) and hold; exit fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Reads as evidence, not rant — the structure itself proves the claim while keeping typography primary.

candidates.metaphor: One person at the center; four nodes around it, every node a negation of a different behavior — all four connected at once.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Relationship diagram fires four simultaneous, mutually exclusive verdicts into one center point: no matter which behavior the center chooses, the surrounding labels cancel it. The spokes show causation is arbitrary, the center never moves.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: One small hub being told four opposite things at the same time — you can't win a game where every answer is wrong.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline top-left, one accent word per pair; node labels stay short and all carry the red accent.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Nodes stagger in around the hub (stagger), each spoke draws (draw), hub pulses once with subtleScale; exit fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Hub-and-spoke is instantly legible and the simultaneity conveys saturation and exhaustion rather than sequence.

candidates.metaphor: Four actions input, one counter climbs 0→4 accusations regardless of input quality, ending on the gold question.
candidates.semanticMechanism: counterChange performs the meaning: each positive act should reset the number, but the counter only increments — cost accumulates while reward never exists. The final headline converts the accumulated count into the existential question.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: The number keeps going up no matter what you do, so the only sane response is the question on screen.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Counter as hero at 140px, WordReveal finale 'JADI… BUAT APA?' with BUAT APA in gold, max two accent words.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Counter ticks with counterChange in four steps synced to labels, indicator dot pulses, finale words reveal then everything fades.
candidates.whyItWorks: A rising number is a physical event; viewers feel the unfairness before decoding the copy.

candidates.metaphor: A four-cell grid of possible behaviors; tapping any cell returns the same hostile verdict — the grid has no positive output.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Grid activeCells hops randomly between all four options while every cell resolves to the red state: the system being probed, not the choice, produces negativity. Exhaustion comes from watching every path fail identically.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: You keep clicking different options and the machine only knows one reply — there's no setting that works.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline top-left with one red accent word; label under grid names the verdict; finale line drops below.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Cells light sequentially (stagger), highlight jumps between cells, all settle red; exit dissolve.
candidates.whyItWorks: Interaction metaphor makes the injustice feel systemic and testable rather than anecdotal.

candidates.metaphor: Four contradictory verdicts arrive as cards and stack into one crushing pile on top of a small circle — the person disappears under their own record.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Stack count grows to 4 while the Circle beneath dims and shrinks: the accumulated labels literally outweigh and occlude the individual. Weight transfer is the argument — meaning is buried by volume of accusation.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Cards keep landing on the little dot until you can't see the dot anymore: the person is gone under other people's words.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline below in lower safe area, gold accent on the final question only; stack carries no extra type.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Cards drop with stagger, Circle dims with subtleScale down, headline reveals last; exit fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Occlusion is unambiguous: viewers see a person vanish under labels without needing to parse a single accusation.

candidates.concept: LEVERS THROW, NEEDLE STAYS AT ZERO
candidates.metaphor: A row of control levers on our side of a thin vertical fence; each lever is thrown fully, yet the readout needle on the fog side stays pinned at zero while the fog drifts on.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Input without coupling: levers animate through full travel while the needle's displacement is exactly zero, so applied effort and target state are physically disconnected.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: We see force applied and no result across the line; the broken link between our action and their thoughts reads instantly as 'this cannot be controlled'.
candidates.typographyStrategy: WordReveal headline (53 chars, 2 lines), red accent on 'nggak' and 'ngontrol'; centered Label under the levers naming the zero readout.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger the lever throws against a highlighted frozen needle, then fade exit; one subordinate background glow behind the fog side.
candidates.whyItWorks: Turns an abstract limit into a measurable zero and quietly stages the next beat, where the one lever that does move is revealed.

candidates.metaphor: One drawn arrow travels toward drifting thought-marks beyond a thin vertical line and stops dead, tip resting on the line, while the targets stay unmoved behind it.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Trajectory arrested at the boundary: the arrow's draw completes but its endpoint equals the barrier coordinate, so the distance to the targets never shrinks no matter how long it draws.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: An arrow unable to finish its own path shows the limit without explaining it; the barrier being only a hairline makes the boundary feel permanent rather than fixable.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline left, max 2 red accent words ('nggak', 'ngontrol'); small Label sits past the barrier where the arrow can never reach.
candidates.motionOpportunity: draw the arrow to the line, highlight the hairline at the halt moment, fade exit.
candidates.whyItWorks: A pure geometric enactment of 'cannot reach' — no icons, no narration needed, and it respects the negative-space rule.

candidates.concept: FAR-SIDE CELLS CHANGE ON THEIR OWN
candidates.metaphor: Across a single hairline, a grid of mind-cells keeps flickering between states unprompted; on our side an input line ends in mid-air, touching nothing.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Autonomous state changes occur with zero input from our side — causality is visibly absent, so the region is outside any reachable control loop.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Cells changing while our side does nothing reads as 'their minds run on their own schedule'; the dangling input line makes the disconnection literal.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Subheadline tier above the split, gold accent on 'nggak akan pernah' as the honest-limit phrase; centered Labels under each half.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger the cell state flips across the grid, subtleScale emphasis on the dangling line end, fade exit.
candidates.whyItWorks: The grid was never used for other people's minds before in this project; autonomous flicker performs 'out of your control' as ongoing behavior.

candidates.metaphor: A control dial on our side of the frame with its transmission line cut clean; turning it spins only our own indicator while the far-side orb keeps its own rhythm.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Rotation is transmitted to nothing: the dial angle changes while the coupled element's state stays constant, letting the viewer watch the causal link fail on every turn.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A dial whose output doesn't follow is the everyday sensation of failed control; the visible cut makes the impossibility structural instead of personal.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Centered headline above the dial, red accent limited to 'nggak' and 'ngontrol'; Label under the cut marks 'terputus'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: positionShift rotation on the dial, static counter-side indicator, single low glow behind the far orb, fade exit.
candidates.whyItWorks: Uses a familiar machine metaphor so the boundary feels like engineering, not a personal shortcoming — supporting the 'sadar batas' emotion.

candidates.metaphor: A counter of our attempts races upward to a high number while beside it a second readout of 'minds changed' never leaves 0, both stacked on one hairline rail.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Asymmetric accumulation: our-side count performs counterChange to maximum while the yield number's value never increments, producing a visible score of zero return.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Two numbers moving in opposite fates is instantly decodable as effort without outcome; the still zero anchors the headline's claim.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline top, gold accent on 'nggak akan pernah'; Labels 'UPAYA' and 'HASIL' beneath the two readouts, left-aligned stack.
candidates.motionOpportunity: counterChange on the attempt counter, highlight pulse on the unchanging zero, fade exit.
candidates.whyItWorks: Numbers make the limit quantitative and cold-clear, differing from every prior lever/barrier/grid metaphor in this project.

candidates.metaphor: Semua suara masuk dari kiri menuju satu bukaan vertikal; lu yang mengatur lebar celahnya, dan hanya aliran tipis yang sampai ke lingkaran HIDUP LU di kanan.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Opini = garis tebal menerjang; celah menyempit dan memotong jumlah yang lolos, suara tertahan meredup, lingkaran kanan tetap tenang. Lebar celah secara harfiah adalah 'seberapa besar'.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Tekanan besar di kiri, bukaan menyempit, area kanan tidak terganggu — penonton langsung melihat bahwa kuasa ada di celah, bukan pada suaranya.
candidates.typographyStrategy: WordReveal 96px uppercase, gold pada 'SEBESAR'; label kecil kiri 'PENDAPAT MEREKA', kanan 'HIDUP LU'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger garis masuk → positionShift celah menyempit → fade suara yang tertahan; muat di 3.6s.
candidates.whyItWorks: Mengubah frasa abstrak 'pengaruh' jadi debit fisik yang terlihat berkurang, tanpa menghapus sumbernya — persis pesan bahwa opini tetap ada, dampaknya yang diatur.

candidates.metaphor: Deret batang intensitas pendapat naik tinggi penuh; satu garis horizontal yang lu set memotongnya — di atas garis hilang, yang tersisa potongan pendek di bawah.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Saat garis kendali turun, puncak batang benar-benar meleleh dan fade, menyisakan potongan yang tingginya persis sama dengan posisi garis: volume yang diizinkan masuk berubah secara nyata.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Batang tinggi terpotong rapi oleh satu garis yang digeser; pemilik garis jelas pemilik kuasa, dan sisa potongan = pengaruh yang diizinkan.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline 96px di atas, accent gold pada 'NGARUH'; label mikro di bawah garis 'YANG LU IZINKAN'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: reveal batang tumbuh → positionShift garis turun → controlledReveal puncak memudar; dua sistem gerak maksimal.
candidates.whyItWorks: MetaphorHint 'skala intensitas yang bisa disetel' direalisasikan sebagai pemotongan ukuran, bukan tombol dekoratif — gambar bicara tanpa teks.

candidates.concept: SPLITTER DIVERTS MOST OF THE FLOW
candidates.metaphor: Satu aliran pendapat masuk dari atas, membentur pemisah bergerak: sebagian besar dialihkan keluar bingkai, hanya sisa kecil diarahkan ke lingkaran HIDUP LU.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Pemisah berputar (positionShift) dan jalur aliran benar-benar berpindah — sudut pemisah menentukan berapa liter yang sampai; suaranya tidak dimatikan, arahnya yang dipilih.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Aliran terbelah di depan mata: mayoritas tumpah keluar frame, sedikit masuk lingkaran — kontrol dipahami sebagai pengalihan, bukan peniadaan.
candidates.typographyStrategy: WordReveal kiri-atas 96px, gold hanya pada 'KENDALI'; label bawah 'ALIRAN YANG SAMPAI'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: draw aliran masuk → positionShift pemisah berputar → fade cabang yang tertahan; exit dissolve.
candidates.whyItWorks: Enaktif hubungan 'opini vs pengaruh' sebagai dua volume terukur; berbeda total dari pintu/dial yang pernah dipakai di proyek sebelumnya.

candidates.concept: THE WORD SHRINKS ACROSS THE LINE
candidates.metaphor: Kata 'PENDAPAT MEREKA' masuk sangat besar dan terang, lalu menyusut serta meredup begitu melewati satu garis rambut — sampai di zona HIDUP LU jadi kecil dan sunyi.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Skala tipografi benar-benar menyusut (scale + fade) setelah melewati garis kendali: suara tidak dihapus, bobotnya di kepala kita yang diperkecil — kontrol diukur pada ukuran kata.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Kata raksasa mendadak jadi kecil setelah garis; penonton membaca bahwa yang diatur bukan keberadaan pendapat tapi besarnya tempatnya di hidup kita.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline dominan 112px lalu kata 'PENDAPAT MEREKA' diskalakan turun; accent gold maks 2 kata; label 34px 'HIDUP LU'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger word-by-word masuk → subtleScale garis menyala → scale kata mengecil lewat garis; exit fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Jenis huruf itu sendiri jadi objek yang diperlakukan — metafora lemah jadi peristiwa visual langsung, cocok untuk beat typographyPriority tinggi.

candidates.metaphor: A single path reaches a junction: a dim stream of dots peels off downward-left while one lit dot keeps straight ahead, the gap between them widening.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The frame literally splits one shared line into two trajectories that never rejoin; viewers watch distance grow, so 'they go home, you continue' is enacted as geometry, not stated.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A fork where one group leaves and one light keeps going reads instantly as 'everyone goes their own way' without reading the headline.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline left-top in two lines, accent on 'hidup lu sendiri'; small label under the continuing dot.
candidates.motionOpportunity: draw the trunk line, stagger the diverging stream away, highlight then hold the single lit dot.
candidates.whyItWorks: Divergence is a physical event the eye follows; the widening gap is the emotional separation.

candidates.metaphor: A full-height hairline splits the frame: left half a crowd of dim dots drifting off-frame, right half one steady dot centered in its own empty space.
candidates.semanticMechanism: The boundary line makes 'their life / your life' two literal compartments; one side empties by motion while the other stays populated and still, performing separation as spatial fact.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Two zones divided by a wall, one emptying and one holding still, reads as 'their world vs mine' at a glance.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline sits in the right compartment, left-aligned, accent on 'lu sendiri'; label small under the lone dot.
candidates.motionOpportunity: reveal the vertical line, fade-slide the dim crowd out left, subtleScale the staying dot.
candidates.whyItWorks: A wall is the most direct non-literal symbol of boundary, and asymmetric motion proves which side is which.

candidates.concept: CROWD GRID WITHDRAWS FROM ONE LIT CELL
candidates.metaphor: A dense grid of dim cells dissolves outward row by row, leaving a single lit cell alone with generous dark negative space around it.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Other people are shown as a uniform field that physically retreats; the remaining lit cell is the only thing left occupying the frame — solitude as the end state of everyone going home.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: When the crowd visibly leaves the picture and one light stays, the message 'you remain with yourself' needs no narration.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline bottom-left above the margin, two lines, one accent word; no paragraph text.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger the grid cells fading outward, then subtleScale the lit cell and hold.
candidates.whyItWorks: Uses negative space as the payload: what empties away is the point, echoing the script's separation.

candidates.metaphor: Dim nodes orbiting one shared center release one by one, each flying off on its own tangent, until a single anchored node and its ring remain.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Belonging is drawn as orbit; leaving is drawn as release along a personal trajectory — the relationship breaks physically, showing others returning to their own lives while you stay centered.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Watched nodes fly away from a common center, viewers decode 'everyone goes back to their own thing' as inevitable motion.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline centered above the diagram, accent on 'hidup mereka'; one short label per released node omitted for calm.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger node releases outward, positionShift the ring, fade the departing nodes.
candidates.whyItWorks: Combines the divergence hint with an orbital system, distinct from door/two-room motifs while keeping low element count.

candidates.concept: OTHERS FLOW PAST, YOU HOLD ANCHOR
candidates.metaphor: A dim stream of arrows sweeps continuously across the upper frame while a single teal dot with a short anchor line stays fixed below in clear space.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Contrast of motion states performs the beat: everyone else is traffic in transit back to their lives, while your position does not move — permanence vs passing is shown by what moves and what doesn't.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Moving crowd against a still point instantly reads 'they leave, you stay with your own life,' even muted.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Caption-style subline top-left, headline bottom-left with accent on 'hidup lu sendiri'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: repeated slide of the arrow stream, controlledReveal of the anchor line, fade the caption in.
candidates.whyItWorks: Adds a time dimension — the traffic keeps going while the anchor never yields, matching 'harus tetap hidup'.

candidates.concept: LANTERN WALKS AWAY FROM THE DIM CROWD
candidates.metaphor: A dim field of crowd dots stays behind while one figure carrying its own light slides away toward open darkness — relief, not rebellion.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Two trajectories diverge: the crowd block never moves, the single lit figure does. Direction + carried light physically show that the crowd's approval stays where it is while the self keeps going.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Even muted, one bright thing leaving a static cluster reads as 'walking away from the crowd' — the light traveling WITH the figure says the warmth comes from inside, not from them.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Left headline top: 'LU NGGAK DICIPTAIN BUAT SEMUA' with accent on 'LU', subline carries the calm resolution.
candidates.motionOpportunity: Grid fades in dim, Circle slides right with a positionShift while its glow holds, everything exits by fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Enacts the metaphorHints directly (figure, lantern, leaving the crowd) without narration; negative space ahead of the figure reads as freedom.

candidates.concept: BAR STALLS AT 87%, THE 'ENOUGH' DOT LIGHTS
candidates.metaphor: An approval bar fills fast, jams short of full, and stays there — while a small gold dot beside it ignites labeled CUKUP.
candidates.semanticMechanism: An unfinished progress bar + a separately lit terminal point shows a capped quantity being declared sufficient: the missing percent is visually present yet no longer matters.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Everyone knows a bar that will not fill. When the gold dot lights anyway, the message decodes instantly: you are not failing the metric, you are done needing it.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline left: 'NGGAK SEMUA ORANG PERLU SUKA' accent on 'NGGAK SEMUA'; Badge reads 'CUKUP' in gold.
candidates.motionOpportunity: counterChange on the bar to 0.87, then highlight/glow on the Indicator dot as the payoff beat.
candidates.whyItWorks: Turns an abstract acceptance into a measurable, visibly stopped process — strong cold-viewer decode, low element count.

candidates.concept: OPINIONS DEFLECT OFF ONE QUIET RING
candidates.metaphor: Dim arrows of opinion converge from every side, strike one calm ring and stop dead, while a single gold arrow leaves the center outward.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Inbound arrows halting at a boundary while one outbound arrow passes through performs control of influence: opinions arrive, none enter, one direction is chosen.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Blocked incoming versus freely outgoing motion is read pre-verbally as 'it doesn't get in — I decide what gets out', matching the emphasis phrase.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline above center: 'PENDAPAT MEREKA BERHENTI DI SINI' accent on 'BERHENTI'; quiet caption below.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger on the three dim arrows, highlight on the ring contact, then the gold arrow's controlledReveal.
candidates.whyItWorks: Directly continues the script's control argument while resolving it — no crowd cliché, geometry carries the meaning.

candidates.concept: DIM CROWD TICKS UNDER ONE HELD GOLD LINE
candidates.metaphor: A row of small identical dim ticks (everyone's opinion) sits beneath one long steady gold line that never bends — typography carries the scene.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Uniform interchangeable marks versus one continuous unique stroke contrasts the many against the singular; the gold line's unbroken hold outlasts every tick, showing identity outlives judgment.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: Ticks read as tally marks of other people; the single unbroken line above them reads as a person who stayed the same regardless.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Large WordReveal headline: 'NGGAK DICIPTAIN BUAT DISENANGI SEMUA' with accent on 'NGGAK DICIPTAIN'; micro-label under the ticks.
candidates.motionOpportunity: stagger reveal on the headline words, draw on the gold line, dim ticks fade last and exit by dissolve.
candidates.whyItWorks: Satisfies high typography priority while the tick-versus-line object pair still enacts the relationship if text is ignored.

candidates.metaphor: A ring target whose bullseye label switches: the center stops being 'SEMUA ORANG' and becomes 'LU', the aim point never moving.
candidates.semanticMechanism: Relabeling the same bullseye shows the goal itself was mis-set: nothing about the world changed, only what counts as the center — self-validation replaced collective approval.
candidates.whyViewerUnderstandsIt: A target with a shrinking audience label is decoded as 'who am I aiming to please?'; when the center names the viewer, relief arrives without explanation.
candidates.typographyStrategy: Headline top-left: 'YANG PUSATNYA BUKAN MEREKA' accent on 'BUKAN MEREKA'; Target label swaps to 'LU'.
candidates.motionOpportunity: controlledReveal on rings, positionShift plus highlight when the label swaps, arrow settles by fade.
candidates.whyItWorks: Fresh metaphor family (aim/goal) absent from project memory; the swap is a single clear event that carries the whole resolution.
